**Alphabet (GOOGL) had the fastest revenue growth between its two most recent fiscal years (FY2024 → FY2025), at 15.1%.**

- **GOOGL:** revenue grew from $350.0 billion to $402.8 billion, a **15.1%** increase (15.09% calculated) — the fastest of the three, edging out Microsoft.
- **MSFT:** revenue grew from $245.1 billion to $281.7 billion, a **14.9%** increase — a close second.
- **AAPL:** revenue grew from $391.0 billion to $416.2 billion, a **6.4%** increase — the slowest of the three.
- Note that the fiscal years cover different calendar months (GOOGL ends December 31, MSFT ends June 30, AAPL ends late September), so the growth rates are not measured over identical periods.

sources.section: Fiscal Year 2024 Compared with Fiscal Year 2023
sources.text:
Revenue increased $33.2 billion or 16% driven by growth across each of our segments. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure. Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased driven by Office 365 Commercial. More Personal Computing revenue increased driven by Gaming.

Cost of revenue increased $8.3 billion or 13% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud and Gaming, offset in part by a decline in Devices.

Gross margin increased $25.0 billion or 17% driven by growth across each of our segments.

- Gross margin percentage increased slightly. Excluding the impact of the change in accounting estimate for the useful lives of our server and network equipment, gross margin percentage increased 2 points driven by improvement in More Personal Computing.

We generate revenue by offering a wide range of cloud-based solutions, content, and other services to people and businesses; licensing and supporting an array of software products; delivering relevant online advertising to a global audience; and designing and selling devices. Our most significant expenses are related to compensating employees; supporting and investing in our cloud-based services, including datacenter operations; designing, manufacturing, marketing, and selling our other products and services; and income taxes.

Highlights from fiscal year 2025 compared with fiscal year 2024 included:

- Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9 billion.

- Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased 14% driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue growth of 15%.

- Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased $10.8 billion or 14%. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 15% with Microsoft 365 Commercial seat growth of 6% driven by small and medium businesses and frontline worker offerings, as well as growth in revenue per user. Microsoft 365 Commercial products revenue grew 7% driven by the Windows Commercial on-premises components of Microsoft 365 suite sales and an increase in Office transactional purchasing with the launch of Office 2024.

- Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased $756 million or 11%. Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue grew 11% driven by Microsoft 365 Consumer subscriber growth of 8% to 89.0 million, as well as growth in revenue per user from the price increase announced in January 2025.

Revenue increased $8.5 billion or 12%.

- Office Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased $5.8 billion or 14%. Office 365 Commercial revenue grew 16% with seat growth of 7%, driven by small and medium business and frontline worker offerings, as well as growth in revenue per user. Office Commercial products revenue declined 16% driven by continued customer shift to cloud offerings.

- Office Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased $237 million or 4%. Microsoft 365 Consumer subscribers grew 10% to 82.5 million.

- LinkedIn revenue increased $1.4 billion or 9% driven by growth across all lines of business – Talent Solutions, Premium Subscriptions, Marketing Solutions, and Sales Solutions.

- Dynamics products and cloud services revenue increased $1.0 billion or 19% driven by Dynamics 365. Dynamics 365 revenue grew 24% driven by growth across all workloads.

As of September 28, 2024 and September 30, 2023, the Company had total deferred revenue of $12.8 billion and $12.1 billion, respectively. As of September 28, 2024, the Company expects 64% of total deferred revenue to be realized in less than a year, 25% within one-to-two years, 9% within two-to-three years and 2% in greater than three years.

EMEA revenue growth was not materially affected by changes in foreign currency exchange rates, as the effect of the U.S. dollar strengthening relative to the Turkish lira was offset by the U.S. dollar weakening relative to the British pound and the euro.

Apple's FY2025 10-K discloses two primary supply chain risk factors in Item 1A: (1) its dependence on outsourcing partners for component and product manufacturing and logistics, many located outside the U.S., and (2) its ability to obtain components in sufficient quantities on commercially reasonable terms.

- **Dependence on outsourced manufacturing and logistics (p.10):** A significant majority of Apple's manufacturing is performed by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam (plus sourcing from U.S. partners and facilities). Apple relies on single-source partners in the U.S., Asia and Europe for many components, and on partners primarily in Asia for final assembly of substantially all of its hardware products, and has outsourced much of its transportation and logistics management. These arrangements lower operating costs but reduce Apple's direct control over production and distribution — diminished control that has from time to time had, and may in the future have, an adverse effect on the cost, quality or quantity of products or its flexibility to respond to changing conditions. Apple also generally remains responsible to the consumer for warranty and out-of-warranty service for product defects, and supplier code of conduct violations occur from time to time and can materially adversely affect its business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition and stock price. The filing adds that changes or additions to the supply chain require considerable time and resources and involve significant risks, including additional regulatory and operational risks.

- **Component availability and single-source dependence (p.11):** Apple's new products often use custom components available from only one source, and components using new technologies may face initial capacity constraints until suppliers' yields mature or capacity increases. Apple may not be able to extend or renew supply agreements on similar terms, or at all, may not obtain sufficient quantities in a timely manner, and may not identify alternative sources. Component suppliers may also fail, be subject to industry consolidation, or concentrate on producing common components rather than Apple's customized ones. As a result, Apple states it remains subject to significant risks of supply shortages and price increases that could materially adversely affect its business, results of operations, financial condition and stock price.

- These risks are corroborated elsewhere in the filing: Item 1 ("Supply of Components," p.6) and the Item 8 note "Concentrations in the Available Sources of Supply of Materials and Product" (p.47) repeat the single-source custom component language, and the Item 8 note confirms that substantially all hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam.

Note: these are the supply-chain risk factors surfaced by the search of the FY2025 10-K; the full Item 1A may contain adjacent risks (e.g., trade or geopolitical matters) not captured in these results.

Sources: [AAPL FY2025 10-K, p.10], [AAPL FY2025 10-K, p.11], [AAPL FY2025 10-K, p.6], [AAPL FY2025 10-K, p.47]

Apple's net income fell by $3.3 billion (3.4%), from $97.0 billion in FY2023 to $93.7 billion in FY2024, and the FY2024 10-K attributes the decline primarily to a one-time income tax charge of $10.2 billion, net, related to the European Commission State Aid Decision.

- **The decline was entirely tax-driven, not operational.** Revenue grew 2.0% to $391.0 billion and operating income rose 7.8% to $123.2 billion (income before provision for income taxes rose to $123.5 billion from $113.7 billion), but the provision for income taxes jumped from $16.7 billion to $29.7 billion, lifting the effective tax rate from 14.7% to 24.1%.
- **Cause per the 10-K:** On September 10, 2024, the European Court of Justice set aside the General Court's 2020 judgment and confirmed the Commission's 2016 State Aid Decision. As a result, in Q4 FY2024 Apple recorded the one-time income tax charge of $10.2 billion, net — $15.8 billion payable to Ireland via release of escrow, partially offset by a U.S. foreign tax credit of $4.8 billion and a decrease in unrecognized tax benefits of $823 million.
- **MD&A commentary:** The Provision for Income Taxes discussion states the 2024 effective tax rate was higher than 2023 "due primarily to a one-time income tax charge of $10.2 billion, net, related to the State Aid Decision, a higher effective tax rate on foreign earnings and lower tax benefits from share-based compensation."
- **Payment details:** As of September 28, 2024, Apple owed €14.2 billion ($15.8 billion) to Ireland, expected to be paid within 12 months, with the settlement funds held in escrow and restricted from general use.
- Despite higher pre-tax income, diluted EPS slipped from $6.13 to $6.08, reflecting the tax charge.

- Note that Microsoft Cloud is not one of Microsoft's three reportable segments (Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, More Personal Computing); it is a cross-segment revenue metric whose amounts are embedded in those segments' product lines.

- Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased $756 million or 11%. - Dynamics products and cloud services revenue increased $996 million or 15% driven by growth in Dynamics 365, offset in part by a decline in Dynamics on-premises products. Dynamics 365 revenue grew 19% with growth across all workloads.

- Gross margin increased $11.2 billion or 13% driven by growth in Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. Gross margin percentage decreased slightly primarily driven by the impact of scaling our AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud.

- Operating expenses increased $1.1 billion or 4% driven by investments in cloud and AI engineering and commercial sales.

meta.query: Microsoft and Alphabet both grew operating income in fiscal year 2025. By how much did each grow, and what does each company's 10-K say drove it?

result.answer:
Google Cloud accounted for 14.6% of Alphabet's total revenue in FY2025, up from 12.4% in FY2024 — an increase of about 2.2 percentage points.

- **FY2025:** Google Cloud revenue was $58.7 billion out of $402.8 billion in consolidated revenues, a 14.6% share (SQL: 14.57%).
- **FY2024:** Google Cloud revenue was $43.2 billion out of $350.0 billion, a 12.4% share (SQL: 12.35%).
- **Why the share rose:** Google Cloud revenue grew 36% (a $15.5 billion increase) while total revenue grew 15%, so Cloud grew faster than the company overall. The FY2025 10-K attributes Cloud's growth primarily to Google Cloud Platform, largely from infrastructure and platform services.
- Shares are of total consolidated revenues, which include a small "Hedging gains (losses)" reconciling item (–$127 million in 2025; $211 million in 2024); the database and the 10-K's segment note (Note 15) report identical figures.
